b2-33-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Lending a Bike
b2-33-01.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks if he can use your bike. You will lend it, but he must look after it.
b2-33-01.prompt: Tell Carlos you will lend him the bike on one strict condition.
cues: Say the condition, that he looks after it
b2-33-01.target: Sí, te la presto siempre y cuando la cuides.
b2-33-01.english: Yes, I will lend it to you provided that you look after it.
b2-33-01.canDo: I can use *siempre y cuando* + subjunctive for a strict condition.

b2-33-02.title: Communicative Challenge: A Trip to the Countryside
b2-33-02.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about the plan for Sunday. You will go to the countryside unless the weather is bad.
b2-33-02.prompt: Tell Meg the plan and the one exception.
cues: Say you will go to the countryside
Say the one exception, the rain
b2-33-02.target: Vamos al campo el domingo a no ser que llueva.
b2-33-02.english: We are going to the countryside on Sunday unless it rains.
b2-33-02.canDo: I can use *a menos que*, *a no ser que* and *salvo que* + subjunctive.

b2-33-03.title: Communicative Challenge: An Unanswered Call
b2-33-03.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says a colleague of his does not answer the phone. You draw a conclusion from that.
b2-33-03.prompt: Tell Carlos what you conclude if the colleague does not answer.
cues: Say what is true: she does not answer
b2-33-03.english: If she does not answer, she must be busy.
b2-33-03.canDo: I can use *si* + indicative to mean "if it is true that".

b2-33-04.title: Communicative Challenge: A Friendly Warning
b2-33-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg often arrives late. You warn her that, if she is late again, you will not let her in.
b2-33-04.prompt: Warn Meg about arriving late again.
cues: Say the condition, in the warning form
b2-33-04.target: Como llegues tarde otra vez, no te dejo entrar.
b2-33-04.english: If you arrive late again, I won't let you in.
b2-33-04.canDo: I can use *como* + present subjunctive to warn someone.

b2-33-05.title: Communicative Challenge: A Missed Party
b2-33-05.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos says he missed a friend's party. You tell him how you feel about the past.
b2-33-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what you wish about the party.
cues: Say what you wish you had done
Say you would have come, had you known
b2-33-05.target: Ojalá hubiera ido; de haberlo sabido, habría venido.
b2-33-05.english: I wish I had gone; had I known, I would have come.
b2-33-05.canDo: I can use *ojalá* + pluperfect subjunctive for a wish about the past.

b2-33-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: A Condition and an Exception
b2-33-consolidation.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks whether you will help with her move. You will help only if she tells you the day, unless you have to work.
b2-33-consolidation.prompt: Tell Meg the condition and the exception.
cues: Say you will help only if she tells you the day
Say the exception, that you have to work
b2-33-consolidation.target: Te ayudo solo si me dices el día, salvo que tenga que trabajar.
b2-33-consolidation.english: I will help you only if you tell me the day, unless I have to work.
b2-33-consolidation.canDo: I can read a short text about Julio Cortázar and his novel.
